knowledge_gaps: The allocation interpretation needs a qualification: reconstruction uses a random target-count denominator. Its finite-batch ratio estimator can change expected gradients when branch sample size changes, even with fixed 0.5/0.5 coefficients. The intervention may therefore affect more than gradient variance.

Checkpoint-linked counters can expose inconsistent documentation but cannot establish which sampler produced an existing checkpoint without matching source/configuration provenance. Historical fixed 64/64 counts must remain distinct from proposed Bernoulli allocation.

No verified baseline-versus-intervention host comparison is supplied. The embedded category selection scores average to 0.5975, but their provenance and equivalence to independent host evaluation are unresolved; they do not demonstrate improvement.

Reproduction still requires the exact terminal cutoff implementation, allocation RNG purpose identifier, baseline configuration identifiers, stopping semantics, and checkpoint-to-accounting linkage. Also distinguish terminal positions in sampled prefixes from full-history endpoints.

Originality 2/10 is reasonable. Potential 6/10 is speculative without ranking or gradient evidence; difficulty 3/10 may underestimate integration and provenance work. Retain the focused experiment, but avoid claiming that it addresses current intent, duplication, or compatibility without corresponding measurements.

The evaluation plan lacks paired uncertainty and an explicit account of prior validation-driven decisions. Fixed seed 42 permits a reproducible comparison but does not establish robustness across training randomness; repeated checkpoint selection also introduces validation selection bias.

follow_up_queries.reason: Clarify whether changing reconstruction batch size changes the expected gradient as well as its variance, without changing the prescribed experiment.
follow_up_queries.query: For masked-item recommendation trained with separately normalized branch losses L=0.5*S_terminal/N_terminal+0.5*S_reconstruction/N_reconstruction, how does finite-sample ratio-estimator bias depend on random numbers of masked targets and correlation between target count and gradients? Compare fixed 64/64 branch counts with 128 Bernoulli(0.75) terminal-view assignments, keeping branch-conditional context distributions unchanged.

follow_up_queries.reason: Specify defensible uncertainty and selection-bias limitations using existing validation outputs while preserving the pinned evaluator and single-model constraint.
follow_up_queries.query: What statistical methods support paired comparison of two sequential recommenders on four-category macro HR@10 with 200 fixed validation users per category and 99 fixed unique negative candidates per user? Explain category-stratified paired user bootstrap intervals, repeated checkpoint-selection bias, and limitations of a single fixed training seed without changing the evaluator or training additional models.
